source.title: Shaping double descent in quantum extreme learning through model design
source.authors: S. Meyer; Ege Yilmaz; Aurélien Lucchi; F. Tacchino; Francesco Scala

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some equations and figure layouts are garbled in the extracted text, but the document is not cut off or the wrong document.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests double-descent behavior in classical linear regression and quantum extreme learning machines, extending the analysis to quantum feature models and design settings.
record.gate_note: Rows record reported risk results and risk curves. Covariance-condition-number and feature-correlation measurements are not rows because they do not measure test risk; the text reports those in Figure 2(a–c), Figures 5–6, and related discussion. Prior-work results and the discussion of effective parameter counting are cited, not tested here. The paper does not sweep training epochs or training-sample count.
record.test_reason: The study derives risk results for linear regression and quantum extreme learning machines and measures test-risk curves while varying readout feature count. Its own results bear on post-interpolation recovery, multiple peaks, and noise-dependent peak suppression.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors connect covariance conditioning to an over-parametrized risk bound and give sufficient correlation conditions for a canonical interpolation threshold. Input strength, reuploads under an injection condition, and appropriately chosen shot noise can improve conditioning and empirical risk. Finite-shot readout can suppress secondary peaks while preserving the interpolation peak. They do not guarantee globally monotonic risk, superiority over the under-parametrized regime, or explain how secondary peaks emerge.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses ridgeless minimum-norm linear regression and fixed quantum feature maps, with sweeps over observable count, circuit design, and measurement shots; it is not a deep-network reproduction.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk and covariance behavior vary with input strength, reupload count, measurement-shot budget, circuit correlation regime, and real-data dataset; circuit depth changes the interpolation-peak height and post-interpolation risk.
record.problems: Several empirical risk outcomes are presented only as figures without numeric values or stated error bars. Real-data risk curves use 90 training samples; results cover a limited set of QELM architectures and datasets. The theoretical reupload result depends on a high-frequency injection condition, and the authors note that they lack a general guarantee that it holds for arbitrary reservoir unitaries.
record.rows_left_out: No reported test-risk result was omitted. Covariance condition-number sweeps in Figure 2(a–c), feature-correlation diagnostics in Figures 5–6, and cited results were excluded because they do not measure test risk.

untested.parts: Model-size sweeps in trained deep networks; QELMs train only a classical linear readout.
Universality beyond the studied feature models; the theoretical formulas do not establish the initial falling segment of a classical U-shaped curve.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count. The correlation criterion is a sufficient condition for threshold stability, not such a measure.
Disappearance of all peaks under optimally tuned regularization; empirical label-noise ablations; a causal explanation of secondary-peak emergence.
Replotting risk against an effective parameter count to recover an ordinary U-shaped curve.

missing.what: Theorem 8 combined with Proposition 1 gives a conditional analytical result restoring R(γ)=σ²/(1−γ) for γ<1 under finite-shot readout. Record its assumptions, including rescaled observable squared norms O(d^−1/2), vanishing cross-observable measurement-variance covariance, and m0=o(√d). This is not an unconditional guarantee for the finite numerical experiments.
missing.locator: Supplementary F4, Theorem 8; C3, Proposition 1; Methods, 'Finite shot noise fixes double descent peaks'

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is warranted from missing curve descriptions alone: remove the proposed V4 scope limitation based on r4–r6 being incompletely described. Likewise, retention of the interpolation peak in r9 does not challenge an optimal-regularization claim that was never tested. The correlated-feature upper bound in r2 should not be treated as an exact observed second descent. Covariance diagnostics already declared in rows_left_out need no additional missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Increasing the number of training samples near interpolation.
Model classes beyond the tested linear regression and QELM settings.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Label-noise-specific causation and disappearance of the peak under optimally tuned conventional regularization.
Whether an appropriate effective parameter count turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: linear regression with i.i.d. Gaussian features
rows.operation_detail: Derive asymptotic expected risk as the feature-to-sample ratio γ varies.
rows.value: For γ < 1, R(γ) = σ²/(1−γ); for γ > 1, the paper gives an explicit asymptotic risk expression and states that risk decreases as γ grows.
rows.locator: Results, “The canonical double descent curve”; Supplementary Section C 2, Theorem 1
rows.note: The paper describes a divergence at the interpolation threshold and a decreasing over-parametrized branch.
rows.check: The formula establishes divergence and recovery immediately beyond interpolation, with the divergent term proportional to label-noise variance. It does not establish an initial descent: σ²/(1−γ) increases throughout γ<1. The increasing bias term also prevents claiming unconditional monotonic decrease throughout γ>1.

rows.subject: linear regression with correlated random features
rows.operation_detail: Analyze risk across under- and over-parametrized regimes under stated feature-correlation conditions.

conditions.value: λmax(Cov(z ⊗ z)) = o(d) for the under-parametrized result

rows.measure: Expected risk and its over-parametrized upper bound
rows.value: For γ < 1, R(γ) = σ²/(1−γ); for γ > 1, the paper gives an upper bound depending on κ(Σ) and states the bound decreases as γ grows.
rows.locator: Results, “Double descent with correlated features”; Supplementary Section C 3, Proposition 1 and Theorem 2
rows.note: The under-parametrized threshold result is conditional on the stated correlation-growth assumption.
rows.check: The under-parametrized risk is exact under the correlation condition, but the over-parametrized result is an asymptotic upper bound, not a measured or exact decreasing risk curve. Include the full-rank, sub-Gaussian, and fixed whitened-norm assumptions. A decreasing variance bound does not prove monotonic total risk.

rows.subject: QELM with unitary 2-design
rows.stage_stated: fixed quantum circuit; classical readout trained
rows.operation_detail: Derive asymptotic quantum risk as the readout feature-to-sample ratio γ varies.
rows.value: The paper reports the canonical double-descent expression: σ²/(1−γ) for γ < 1 and an explicit over-parametrized expression for γ > 1.
rows.note: The paper also notes that this 2-design setting is not scalable for its stated practical target-function regime.
rows.check: Corollary 1 additionally assumes feature-matrix ranks, a realizable teacher, and the specified cross-input state overlaps. As in r1, the formula supports interpolation divergence and subsequent recovery, not an initial descent or unconditional monotonic recovery at every larger capacity.
